_expect.name: Old Aid Wall aka Upper Echelon Wall

co_old_aid_wall_aka_upper_echelon_wall.blurb: A steep, streaked wall in the Triple Tier Area of Poudre Canyon, west of Fort Collins, sitting on the south side of the highway at roughly 6,100 feet. It holds a dozen single-pitch lines of about 65 to 90 feet, nearly all of them bolted. The grades lean hard: one easy-ish line near 5.9, a few in the 5.10s and low 5.11s, and a strong cluster in the 5.12s with a couple of 5.13s on top. A single crack line takes gear. The face leans north, and the rock is dense with little texture, so expect powerful, overhanging moves rather than a beginner crag.

co_punk_rock_aka_poacher_s_rock.blurb: A small, compact crag among the Ironclads in the Estes Park Valley, between Estes Park and Boulder. Walls top out near 30 feet, so these are short, bolted faces that also suit top-roping. Most of the dozen climbs are sport lines from the high 5.7s through the 5.10s, with a couple of 5.11s and one gear route. The granite is rough and textured; holds are positive but hard on the skin, and loose grit can collect on ledges at the base. Crowds are light, shade creeps in during the afternoon, and the elevation keeps summer days cooler. Good for a relaxed day of moderate mileage.

co_catacomb_the.blurb: A walkway-like corridor between rock formations in the Monastery, high above Big Thompson Canyon near Estes Park, with the Boneyard on one side and the Sepulcher on the other. Twelve routes, mostly sport with some trad, run from the 5.8 range up to the low 5.12s, with the bulk in the 5.8 to 5.11 band. The pegmatite is crystalline and edgy, with knobs, crimps and smoother slabs, so footwork matters. West-facing stone heats up fast, making midsummer afternoons uncomfortable. Reaching it takes a hike in from the road; descent to some routes is on loose, uneven trail, so wear sturdy shoes.
